correctness.rationale: For every admissible target and coupling, unit-sphere support converts the cost to 2-2 E<X,Y>. Since X lies in U and the target has second moment I/d, L2 Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the correlation by sqrt(r/d). The explicit orthogonal lift has unit norm and exactly isotropic second moment, so it attains the bound. Equality in Hilbert-space Cauchy--Schwarz forces P_U Y=sqrt(r/d)X; the remaining tightness blocks are exactly E[ZZ^T]=P_{U^perp}/(d-r) and E[XZ^T]=0. The r=d endpoint is immediate.

originality.rationale: The exact spherical distance and optimal-coupling classification are not implied by the closest-full-rank push-forward theorem, because the source moment here is singular when r<d and the target is constrained to the unit sphere. The 2018 spherical paper leaves the general expression open. The 2025 frame-operator work supplies the same matrix lower bound after continuous extension to positive semidefinite moments, but not a sphere-preserving fixed-source attainment or the equality coupling structure. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no covering statement.
residual_risks: The 2024 dissertation full text was not materially inspected, so an equivalent special case hidden beyond its abstract remains a priority risk.
An unindexed optimal-transport or directional-statistics source could state the same singular spherical attainment without probabilistic-frame terminology.

value.rationale: The spherical closest-tight-frame problem is explicitly left open in the motivating literature. This theorem solves a natural all-dimensions rank-deficient family exactly, extends the known Dirac-type endpoint to every subspace-isotropic source, and gives the complete geometry of equality couplings. The result is structurally useful because it identifies how much orthogonal second moment must be added and shows that the matrix lower bound is sharply attainable despite the sphere constraint.
